static_traits.name: Chen Mei
static_traits.social_status: Weak social support, few people to confide in
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not yet sought counseling or treatment; has not yet encountered similar psychological problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Fairly cooperative, slightly tense, expresses clearly, strong logicality, able to describe automatic thoughts and distress in detail

basic_info.main_problem: Since being hired as a security guard, I always feel people see me as lazy, as someone who just wants to sleep on the job; this feeling of being misunderstood arises frequently at work and disrupts my focus and performance.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these thoughts are affecting my mental health and job satisfaction; I hope that next time we can focus on discussing how to catch and challenge the negative thoughts when they appear.

core_beliefs: Others look down on me (especially because my job is not respectable enough)

special_situations.event: Every time she enters the workplace and interacts with colleagues or the people she guards
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I work in a job considered low-status, others will look down on me and think I am lazy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proving my diligence and value through overtime and taking on extra tasks
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am lazy and only want to sleep at work

special_situations.event: After work, while lying in bed at home preparing to sleep, recalls the day's interactions and has difficulty falling asleep
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Without clear and frequent praise, it means they are gossiping behind my back that I am incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeping distance from colleagues, reducing communication to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are probably all saying behind my back that I am incapable

special_situations.event: A supervisor or colleague gives positive feedback (such as thanking her for overtime, saying they feel more at ease with her on duty)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If praise isn't sustained or strong, it's just politeness and doesn't count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Disqualifying positive information, continuing to seek proof through more work
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They're just being polite, not genuinely recognizing me

special_situations.event: Sees others having higher education or more respectable positions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my job isn't respectable enough, I am not good enough and don't deserve respect
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-criticism; demands self work harder to 'make up for it'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My job is inferior to others', so I will be looked down on

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be respected and genuinely seen (hopes my work and effort are recognized)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being looked down on, being labeled 'lazy/incapable' and excluded
defense_goal: Gaining recognition through overtime and taking on more responsibility, easing the fear of being looked down on
Keeps a certain distance from others to reduce the risk of being evaluated and maintain safety

object_relations.self_representation: Not-respectable, not-good-enough worker, someone easily looked down on
object_relations.object_representation: Others who are judgmental and contemptuous (colleagues, those under his protection, the outside world)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to accept positive feedback and explore alternative explanations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding others' praise as insincere politeness, thus maintaining the inner narrative that 'others look down on me'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone reserved, speaks softly, uses phrasing like 'They were just being polite' to downplay praise; avoids lingering emotionally for long on the experience of being recognized.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing interactions with colleagues or topics of feeling judged
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Projecting inner inferiority and insecurity into others' intent: 'they look down on me and gossip about me behind my back'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using expressions like 'they all think / they might be saying...', defensive tone, keeping social distance, reducing detailed exploration.

manifestations: At work, tending to keep distance from colleagues and be alone because of feeling judged
Insecurity about 'job not respectable enough' and 'education not good enough', questioning self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses society's standards for occupational status as the measure of self-worth ('I should have a better job / more education')
Taking external stereotypes of the security-guard profession directly as fact and internalizing them into self-evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism ('I am not good enough')
In socializing, deliberately keeps distance and is cautious in words and actions out of worry about being judged

exception_events.target_problem: At work, Chen Mei typically thinks others look down on her, labeling herself lazy, thus feeling anxious and avoiding interaction with colleagues.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last month her supervisor thanked her for overtime, and colleagues said they felt safer with her on duty; this provided evidence of positive evaluation and recognition of her work, differing from the previous dominant narrative of 'others look down on me'.
exception_events.reason: Different support: the supervisor's thanks and colleagues' expressions of feeling safe, forming concrete cues of positive external feedback.

positive_force: Willing to try cognitive reappraisal and behavioral experiments
Strong sense of work responsibility, proactively works overtime and takes on extra tasks
Having received positive feedback from supervisors and colleagues (recognition and a sense of security)
Positive attitude toward counseling; willing to practice positive self-talk
negative_force: Overly concerned with external evaluation; seeks external validation
Negative cognitive patterns such as mind reading and overgeneralization
Self-criticism and shame leading to a low sense of self-worth
Sleep disturbed, further weakening work performance and emotional stability

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly engaging in 'mind reading' and self-denying negative thinking at work, accompanied by anxiety and disrupted focus
antecedent: Going to work, contact with colleagues or those under one's care
When thinking about one's education and professional status
target_behavior.core_reason: Insecurity about 'job not respectable enough' and high reliance on external evaluation, fearing being labeled 'lazy/incapable'.
target_behavior.function: Escaping the threat of negative evaluation, subjectively maintaining predictability of the external world (reducing uncertainty through self-protective anticipation).
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, damaged relationships, sleep disturbance and worsened anxiety.

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding interaction with colleagues at work, tending to be alone
antecedent: When feeling judged or belittled by others
When lacking clear positive feedback at the moment
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying that contact with others will expose 'not being good enough', hence choosing withdrawal to reduce anxiety.
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential negative evaluations and social pressure, relieving tension in the short term.
target_behavior.consequence: Alienated interpersonal relationships, weak support system, further reinforcing the subjective experience of being looked down on.
